_comment: 20 fixture GitHub issues for `npm run setup` seeding + `npm run demo`. Ground-truth fields (expected_classification, expected_priority_band, golden_response) are used by the Agent Society benchmark to score accuracy and voice similarity. The demo targets fix-001 by default (DEMO_FIXTURE_ID).

issues.title: Segfault when parsing a file that starts with a null byte
issues.body:
## Description
The parser crashes with a segfault when the input file begins with a `\0` byte.

## Steps to reproduce
```js
const { parse } = require('fastlane-parser');
const fs = require('fs');
fs.writeFileSync('bad.lane', '\0lane v1');
parse(fs.readFileSync('bad.lane')); // boom
```

## Expected
It should throw a `ParseError`, not crash the whole process.

## Actual
```
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

## Environment
- fastlane-parser: 2.4.1
- node: v20.11.0
- macOS 14.4
issues.author: ravi-codes
issues.golden_response: Thanks for the clear repro, @ravi-codes — that's a real one. A leading null byte slips past the header scan in `src/lexer.ts` and we end up indexing past the buffer. We should be raising a `ParseError` there, never segfaulting. I'll get a guard in for the next patch. In the meantime you can pre-strip control bytes as a workaround. Appreciate the report!

issues.title: Memory keeps growing when reconnecting the websocket watcher
issues.body:
When I use `watch()` with auto-reconnect enabled, RSS climbs by ~5MB every time the socket drops and reconnects. Over a day it OOMs the process. Looks like the old listeners aren't being removed on reconnect.

Version 2.4.0, node 18.
issues.author: mei-li
issues.golden_response: Good catch, and thanks for sticking with the debugging @mei-li. That sounds like we're re-adding the `data` listener on every reconnect without tearing down the previous one in `src/watcher.ts`. I'll wire up a teardown on `close`. If you can confirm the leak disappears when you call `unwatch()` before reconnecting, that'd help confirm the theory.

issues.title: Add a dark mode to the docs site
issues.body: Love the library! The docs site is bright white though. Could we get a dark mode toggle? Happy to help if you point me at the theme files.
issues.author: nightowl-dev
issues.golden_response: Appreciate the kind words @nightowl-dev! A dark mode is a nice idea. The docs theme lives in `docs/theme/` and the palette is a single CSS variables block — a toggle would mostly be a second block plus a button. If you'd like to open a PR I'm happy to review it; otherwise I'll queue it up.

issues.title: How do I set a custom parse timeout?
issues.body: I have some very large `.lane` files and the default timeout seems too short. Is there a way to configure the timeout?
issues.author: curious-cat
issues.golden_response: Hey @curious-cat — yes, pass `{ timeoutMs }` as the second argument to `parse()`, e.g. `parse(buf, { timeoutMs: 30000 })`. Default is 5000ms. It's in the API docs under Options, though I admit it's easy to miss — I'll make it more prominent.

issues.title: App crashes with a segfault when the file starts with a null byte
issues.body: When I open a file that starts with a null byte, the parser crashes with a segfault instead of throwing an error. The whole process dies with a segmentation fault — no ParseError, no stack trace, just gone. The file begins with a null byte and everything segfaults. Using fastlane-parser 2.4.1, node 20.
issues.author: puzzled-pat
issues.golden_response: Hi @puzzled-pat — this looks like the same crash as #101 (segfault on a leading null byte). I'm going to close this as a duplicate and track the fix there; please subscribe to #101 for updates. Thanks for reporting!

issues.title: Race condition: cache returns stale entry right after invalidate()
issues.body:
If I call `invalidate(key)` and then `get(key)` in the same tick, I sometimes still get the old value. Looks like invalidation is async but not awaited internally. Repro is flaky — maybe 1 in 20 runs.

```js
cache.set('k', 1);
cache.invalidate('k');
console.log(cache.get('k')); // sometimes prints 1
```
v2.3.9, node 20.
issues.author: concurrency-carol
issues.golden_response: Thanks @concurrency-carol, and nice minimal repro. You're right that `invalidate()` schedules the eviction on a microtask but `get()` reads synchronously, so there's a window. I think the fix is to drop the entry from the map synchronously and only defer the listener notification. I'll take a look this week.

issues.title: Support YAML config in addition to JSON
issues.body: Right now `.fastlanerc` must be JSON. A lot of our other tooling uses YAML. Could the loader also accept `.fastlanerc.yaml`?
issues.author: yaml-fan
issues.golden_response: Reasonable ask @yaml-fan. The config loader is in `src/config.ts` and already abstracts the parse step, so adding a YAML branch behind an optional `yaml` peer dep would be clean. I'd want to keep YAML optional so we don't add weight for JSON-only users. PR welcome if you want to take it.

issues.title: Dates parsed one day off in non-UTC timezones
issues.body:
When I parse a lane with a `date: 2026-03-10` field while my machine is on `America/Los_Angeles`, the resulting Date is `2026-03-09`. Looks like you're constructing the Date without forcing UTC.

v2.4.1.
issues.author: tz-tina
issues.golden_response: Yep, that's a bug @tz-tina — we're doing `new Date('2026-03-10')` which is UTC midnight, then formatting in local time. We should parse date-only fields as UTC and keep them UTC throughout. Thanks for pinning down the timezone; that's usually the hard part.

issues.title: Does parse() support streaming large files?
issues.body: I have multi-GB `.lane` files. Can I stream them through `parse()` or does it load everything into memory?
issues.author: bigdata-bob
issues.golden_response: Right now `parse()` is buffer-based, so it loads the whole file. For multi-GB inputs you'd want `createParseStream()` (added in 2.2) which yields records as it goes. Docs are thin on it — I'll expand the streaming section. Let me know if the stream API covers your case.

issues.title: CLI hangs forever on files larger than ~500MB
issues.body: `fastlane parse big.lane` just sits there with no output and never exits when the file is bigger than about half a gig. Have to ctrl-C. Smaller files are fine. v2.4.0.
issues.author: ops-olu
issues.golden_response: Thanks @ops-olu. A hang on large files usually means we're buffering the whole thing and blocking the event loop — the CLI should be using the streaming parser for big inputs and it probably isn't. I'll check the size threshold in `src/cli.ts`. As a workaround, `--stream` forces the streaming path if you're on 2.4.

issues.title: Add retry with exponential backoff to the remote loader
issues.body: `loadRemote(url)` fails immediately on a transient 503. Could we add configurable retries with exponential backoff?
issues.author: resilient-rae
issues.golden_response: Sensible @resilient-rae. I'd add a `{ retries, backoffMs }` option to `loadRemote` defaulting to 0 retries so we don't change current behavior silently. Exponential with jitter is the way. Happy to review a PR, or I'll get to it after the 2.5 work.

issues.title: Security: API key is written to the debug log in plaintext
issues.body:
When `DEBUG=fastlane:*` is set, `loadRemote` logs the full request including the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header. That key ends up in CI logs. This is a security problem.

v2.4.1.
issues.author: sec-sam
issues.golden_response: Thank you for flagging this privately-worthy issue @sec-sam — agreed this is a security bug and it's top of my list. We should be redacting `Authorization` (and any `*token*`/`*key*` header) before anything hits the debug logger in `src/net.ts`. I'll ship a patch release and add a redaction test so it can't regress. Please let me know if you've seen it leak anywhere beyond the request logger.

issues.title: Vulnerable transitive dependency: lodash <4.17.21
issues.body: `npm audit` flags a prototype pollution advisory in lodash pulled in transitively. Could you bump the dependency that brings in the old lodash?
issues.author: audit-aanya
issues.golden_response: Thanks @audit-aanya. The old lodash comes in through `some-templating-dep`; I'll bump that to a version that pulls lodash ^4.17.21 and add an `overrides` entry as a belt-and-suspenders. Dependency advisories like this go out as a patch release quickly. Appreciate you keeping an eye on the audit.

issues.title: RSS grows unbounded under load
issues.body: Our service that uses the websocket watcher slowly eats all memory until it's killed. Restarting fixes it temporarily. Seems related to reconnects.
issues.author: prod-priya
issues.golden_response: Hi @prod-priya — this is almost certainly the same leak as #102 (listeners not torn down on websocket reconnect). I'll close this as a duplicate and track it on #102, which already has a repro. Subscribe there for the fix.

issues.title: Add HMAC signature verification for the webhook receiver
issues.body: The `createWebhookReceiver()` helper accepts any payload. It'd be great if it verified an HMAC signature header so we can trust the source.
issues.author: secure-sven
issues.golden_response: Good idea @secure-sven. I'd add an optional `{ secret }` to `createWebhookReceiver()` and verify the signature with a timing-safe compare, rejecting with 401 on mismatch. Keeping it optional preserves backward-compat. This is the kind of thing I'd merge quickly if you want to send a PR.

issues.title: How can I contribute?
issues.body: I'd love to help out with the project. Where should I start? Is there a contributing guide?
issues.author: eager-ed
issues.golden_response: Welcome @eager-ed, and thank you! There's a `CONTRIBUTING.md` in the root that covers setup and the test workflow. Issues tagged `good first issue` are the best place to start — #103 (docs dark mode) and #109 (YAML config) are both approachable. Ping me on any of them and I'll help you get going.

issues.title: Unicode filenames break the file resolver on Windows
issues.body:
If a `.lane` file has a non-ASCII name like `café.lane`, `resolve()` throws `ENOENT` on Windows even though the file exists. Works on macOS/Linux.

```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'caf\xc3\xa9.lane'
```
v2.4.1, Windows 11.
issues.author: win-wendy
issues.golden_response: Thanks @win-wendy — that's a Windows encoding issue. We're likely passing a mis-encoded path to `fs.open`; the bytes in your error are UTF-8 for `é`, so something is double-encoding. I'll need to normalize to the platform's expected encoding in `src/resolve.ts`. I don't have a Windows box handy, so if you can test a patch I'd appreciate it.
